title: Multi-AZ 3-Tier Highly Available Web Application
scenario: A company needs to host a mission-critical web application with zero single points of failure across multiple Availability Zones, automated scaling during traffic spikes, and isolated database tier.
keyTakeaways: ALB distributes incoming HTTPS traffic across EC2 instances in multiple AZs.
Public subnets only contain Load Balancer and NAT Gateways; EC2 instances live in Private subnets.
Amazon Aurora replicates 6 storage copies across 3 AZs with automatic sub-30s failover.
diagramMermaid:
graph TD
    User["Global Users"] --> WAF["AWS WAF"]
    WAF --> R53["Route 53 DNS"]
    R53 --> ALB["Application Load Balancer"]

    subgraph VPC["AWS VPC (Multi-AZ)"]
        subgraph AZ_A["Availability Zone A"]
            ALB_A["ALB Node A"]
            NAT_A["NAT Gateway A"]
            EC2_A["EC2 Web/App Instance"]
            DB_Primary[("Aurora Primary DB")]
        end

        subgraph AZ_B["Availability Zone B"]
            ALB_B["ALB Node B"]
            NAT_B["NAT Gateway B"]
            EC2_B["EC2 Web/App Instance"]
            DB_Replica[("Aurora Read Replica")]
        end
    end

    ALB --> ALB_A
    ALB --> ALB_B
    ALB_A --> EC2_A
    ALB_B --> EC2_B
    EC2_A --> DB_Primary
    EC2_B --> DB_Primary
    DB_Primary -.->|Auto Replication| DB_Replica

title: Serverless Event-Driven Microservices Architecture
scenario: An e-commerce platform needs to process high volume customer orders, execute asynchronous validation, process payments, and notify logistics partners with zero server management and pay-per-use billing.
keyTakeaways: API Gateway provides low-latency REST endpoints with built-in throttling and Cognito authentication.
Lambda scales instantly to zero without idle server cost.
EventBridge routes order events to decoupled consumers (Payment, Inventory, Notification) asynchronously.
SQS Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) capture failed events for retry and auditing.
diagramMermaid:
graph LR
    Client["Web / Mobile Client"] --> APIGW["API Gateway"]
    APIGW --> OrderFn["Order Processing Lambda"]
    OrderFn --> OrdersTable[("DynamoDB Orders Table")]
    OrderFn --> Bus["Amazon EventBridge Event Bus"]

    subgraph EventConsumers["Decoupled Event Consumers"]
        Bus -->|OrderPlaced| PayQueue["Payment SQS"]
        PayQueue --> PayFn["Payment Lambda"]

        Bus -->|OrderPlaced| InvQueue["Inventory SQS"]
        InvQueue --> InvFn["Inventory Lambda"]

        Bus -->|OrderPaid| NotifyFn["Customer Notification Lambda"]
        NotifyFn --> SNS["Amazon SNS / SES"]
    end

    PayQueue -.->|DLQ on failure| DLQ[("Dead Letter Queue")]

title: Disaster Recovery: Warm Standby with Route 53 & Aurora Global Database
scenario: A financial services enterprise requires cross-region disaster recovery for catastrophic regional outages with RTO < 5 minutes and RPO < 1 second.
keyTakeaways: Aurora Global Database uses dedicated storage-level replication (< 1s latency) without database compute load.
Secondary region maintains a scaled-down fleet of EC2/ECS instances (Warm Standby) ready to auto-scale immediately.
Route 53 Active-Passive DNS failover automatically reroutes global traffic upon primary health check failure.
diagramMermaid:
graph TD
    Users["Global Users"] --> R53["Route 53 DNS Failover"]

    subgraph PrimaryRegion["Primary Region (us-east-1) - ACTIVE"]
        ALB_Pri["Primary ALB"]
        ASG_Pri["Full Scale Auto Scaling Group"]
        Aurora_Pri[("Aurora Global Primary DB")]
        S3_Pri["Primary S3 Bucket"]
    end

    subgraph SecondaryRegion["Secondary Region (us-west-2) - WARM STANDBY"]
        ALB_Sec["Standby ALB"]
        ASG_Sec["Scaled-Down Standby ASG"]
        Aurora_Sec[("Aurora Global Secondary DB")]
        S3_Sec["Replica S3 Bucket"]
    end

    R53 -->|Health Check OK - Primary| ALB_Pri
    R53 -.->|Failover| ALB_Sec

    ALB_Pri --> ASG_Pri
    ASG_Pri --> Aurora_Pri
    ALB_Sec --> ASG_Sec
    ASG_Sec --> Aurora_Sec

    Aurora_Pri ==>|Fast Storage Replication| Aurora_Sec
    S3_Pri ==>|S3 CRR| S3_Sec

title: Decoupled Asynchronous Fanout Architecture (SNS + SQS)
scenario: An image processing application receives user uploads that must be concurrently resized, analyzed for content moderation, watermarked, and archived without blocking user requests.
keyTakeaways: S3 triggers SNS Topic upon PutObject upload.
SNS Fans out the event to multiple independent SQS Queues simultaneously.
Each worker queue processes at its own pace without affecting other pipelines.
Loose coupling protects downstream systems from traffic spikes.
diagramMermaid:
graph LR
    User["User App"] -->|Upload Image| S3["Amazon S3 Bucket"]
    S3 -->|S3 Event Notification| SNS["Amazon SNS Topic"]

    SNS -->|Fanout Message| Q1["Resize SQS Queue"]
    SNS -->|Fanout Message| Q2["Moderation SQS Queue"]
    SNS -->|Fanout Message| Q3["Watermark SQS Queue"]

    Q1 --> L1["Resize Lambda Worker"]
    L1 --> S3_Thumb["S3 Thumbnails"]
    Q2 --> L2["Rekognition Lambda Worker"]
    L2 --> DynamoDB[("Safety Log DB")]
    Q3 --> L3["Watermark Lambda Worker"]
    L3 --> S3_Watermarked["S3 Watermarked"]

title: Enterprise Hybrid Cloud Networking with AWS Transit Gateway
scenario: An enterprise needs to connect on-premises data centers to dozens of AWS VPCs (Production, Development, Shared Services) with centralized routing, transitive VPC-to-VPC communication, and centralized Internet egress.
keyTakeaways: AWS Transit Gateway replaces full-mesh VPC Peering with a hub-and-spoke star topology.
Supports transitive routing between On-Premises, VPCs, and Centralized Inspection VPCs.
AWS Direct Connect with VPN backup provides high-speed dedicated hybrid connectivity with automatic failover.
diagramMermaid:
graph TD
    subgraph OnPrem["On-Premises Data Center"]
        Router["Corporate Edge Router"]
    end

    subgraph AWSCloud["AWS Global Cloud"]
        TGW["AWS Transit Gateway (Hub & Spoke Router)"]

        subgraph ProdVPC["Production VPC"]
            ProdAttach["VPC Attachment"] --> ProdEC2["Production Workloads"]
        end

        subgraph DevVPC["Development VPC"]
            DevAttach["VPC Attachment"] --> DevEC2["Development Workloads"]
        end

        subgraph SharedVPC["Centralized Security & Egress VPC"]
            SharedAttach["VPC Attachment"] --> FW["AWS Network Firewall"]
            FW --> NAT["NAT Gateway"]
            NAT --> IGW["Internet Gateway"]
        end
    end

    Router ==>|Direct Connect| TGW
    Router -.->|VPN Backup| TGW

    TGW <--> ProdAttach
    TGW <--> DevAttach
    TGW <--> SharedAttach
